purpose: Current React boundaries and retained source UI contracts for future frontend rewrites. This is an engineering design map, not an execution log or a completion claim.

currentImplementation.frontend: React and TypeScript shared by browser and Electron
currentImplementation.backend: ASP.NET Core HTTP server with isolated retained C# workers

uiMounts.mount: ProjectExplorerControl → ProjectExplorerMainPageTiled → FirstLaunchScreen / ProjectOpenProjectDialog / NewProjectPage
uiMounts.stateOwner: RecentProjectRecord entries live in browser localStorage under hec-ras-web.project.recent.v1 and are added only after a successful open. NewProjectDraft, including createDirectory, is modal-local and resets with resetKey; its initial directory is empty.
readActions: workspace upload when BackendGateway.uploadWorkspace is available
uiMounts.writeBoundary: project.create receives the user-entered absolute parent directory on the C# Host, not a browser-local directory. Its returned projectPath/projectXml/revision become the active context only if the original session/path/XML/revision still match. Directory selection is not persisted as a default start directory.

uiMounts.mount: MapFeaturePage → MapDocumentTabs → NewMapFlyout
uiMounts.stateOwner: The create request captures projectSessionID/projectPath/projectRevision/projectXml plus the saved visualizationRevision. Map kind, menu open state, busy state and request generation are local to the flyout.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: map.document.create writes a saved map document into .vis using projectXmlSHA and expectedVisualizationRevision. The UI validates map type/index/name and the previous/new visualization revisions before installing the tab; a tree refresh must match the saved revision. It does not save the .ras project.

uiMounts.mount: MapFeaturePage → VectorSymbologyEditor (separate legacy conditional evaluator/preview control; persisted map rendering is described by map-vector-symbology-renderer)
uiMounts.stateOwner: The owner key binds project session/path/revision, active map, exact tree node, canonical vector path and the validated source SHA. Feature-index selection and conditional rules are page-local drafts; evaluation receipts are accepted only for the same owner, revision and draft key.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: vector.symbology.inspect/evaluate only inspects attributes and returns the legacy C# conditional-evaluation preview; this control does not save .vis styles or apply its result to the map. The separately mounted VectorLayerStyleEditor and useMapVectorRendering own persisted map styles and styled rendering. This control retains its local dirty-owner switching behavior.

uiMounts.mount: ResultsWorkspace → ResultNodeDetails → DetailedResultHeader / ResultPlanAssociationsViewer / ResultTerrainAssociation / PlanNodeDetails
uiMounts.stateOwner: Details bind to the selected Result path/revision and current project path/XML/revision. Async detail and save generations also bind to the active result owner. Result metadata, associations, candidates and embedded settings are server snapshots. PlanNodeDetails owns a local descriptionDraft under planDescriptionOwner (project session/path plus Result path/revision) and reports its dirty state. ResultsWorkspace keeps imported user-dataset edits under a separate project-scoped results-user-dataset key in the in-memory ResultsDraftStore; its dirty owner is reported only while that user dataset is active.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: Only an eligible embedded Plan description is writable through result.planSettings.save, when Result/HDF and project revisions match, a parent context commit callback exists, the Plan identity matches and there are no other dirty owners. The Plan description owner is excluded from the other-draft check so its own edit can be saved; any separate dirty owner, including an active imported user-dataset draft, blocks the save. Cancel/Discard in PlanNodeDetails restores the server-saved description. The imported user dataset Restore resets to its in-memory original import, while CSV export adopts the exported data as a new local baseline; neither writes the HDF. The Plan save receipt updates the selected Result revision and writes the Result HDF, not .ras. Result terrain associations, Plan associations, candidate lists, embedded fields and images remain read-only.

uiMounts.mount: MapTimeAxis → MultiResultNodeDetails when the active map tree node is MultiResult
uiMounts.stateOwner: Comparison selection groups and their selected Result paths/revisions belong to the current useMapResultFrames map/workflow owner. The control is absent for non-MultiResult nodes.
readActions: map result source/tree and frame reads through useMapResultFrames
uiMounts.writeBoundary: Add/remove changes only the current map-session comparison selection; the controller caps the set at 32 and revalidates sources. It does not write .vis or create a second result session.

uiMounts.mount: EditorWorkbench → SchemaFieldRenderer → InputDateTimePropertyItem / DateTimeInputBox / DateInputBox
uiMounts.stateOwner: Schema date fields call the same EditorWorkbench onFieldChange path as other source fields. The controls keep the source text value; recognized wall-clock forms preserve their separator and zone suffix, and unrecognized forms stay visible as raw text. TimeSeriesPayloadDateTimeColumn is a read-only result-row label.
readActions: model.load/schema snapshot; no date control request of its own
uiMounts.writeBoundary: Date text changes remain in the current model draft and reach HDF only through model.save after normal validation. The dedicated BoundaryConditionTimeWindow still uses datetime-local conversion and writes the grouped boundary-time values into the same draft; it is not the timezone-neutral text control.

uiMounts.mount: EditorWorkbench → BoundaryConditionEditor → BoundaryConditionLineEditorPage → DetailedBoundaryConditionHeader / BoundaryConditionTimeWindow / BoundaryConditionLineAndPayloadPickerPage → BCLinesLayerActiveFeatures / BoundaryConditionLineEditor → BCLineLayerLastSelectedFeatureLineEditor / BoundaryConditionLinePayloadsList / NewPayloadDialog → NewPayloadPage → ExternalConnectionLinker / payload editors
uiMounts.stateOwner: The selected model session, source path/revision and ModelDraft own line fields, aliases, rows, samples, payload values and transform sourceState. BoundaryConditionLineAndPayloadPickerPage derives selection from snapshot lines and keeps the current line in local view state using the stable snapshot line GUID; its detail projection does not mutate the parent draft or save baseline. PayloadListItem only highlights the snapshot/draft selectedPayloadId; it does not invent a selection callback. For Remote payloads, ExternalConnectionLinker receives only the Host-provided NewPayloadPage/ViewModel_SelectedExternalConnection choices and holds no separate connection owner.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: The selected line name and payload fields/tables remain parent ModelDraft edits. Payload create/remove uses model.boundaryTransform and accepts only a revision-matched draft projection with changed sourceState and stable payload IDs; field, date/time, table and sample edits stay in the same draft. ExternalConnectionLinker selects an existing connection ID through the existing setValue("SelectedExternalConnection", id) path; NewPayloadDialog validation, parent transform and model.save remain authoritative. The linker does not import or create connections and explicitly reports that limitation. Line selection is view-only. Only parent model.save commits the model HDF. Source-level contract only; no batch-9 build or runtime acceptance is claimed.

uiMounts.mount: GeometryEditor → GeometryCulvertsPage → CulvertsEditor → CulvertsTable / CulvertEditor / barrel and opening property pages
uiMounts.stateOwner: The Geometry workbench owns project/model identity, captured HDF revision, stable culvert row IDs, draftState and undo state. Selected rows and the active subpage are view state.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: geometry.culverts.edit returns a revision-bound server draft for edits/add/remove/commands; it does not commit the HDF. The Geometry parent model.save includes geometryCulvertState and advances the selected asset only after its save response. Local-only rows/overrides remain unsaved and block parent persistence.

uiMounts.mount: EditorWorkbench → TerrainLayersEditor → selected terrain-input detail/table editors; loaded ChannelMod input → ChannelModTerrainInputProperties → ChannelModTopologyEditor; loaded PolygonRasterModTerrainInput → TerrainPolygonMapEditor
uiMounts.stateOwner: The current model owner and ModelDraft hold terrainView, rows, selections, validation state and sourceState. Generic terrain picker/creator, stats and feature-table controls operate on the selected Host input. ChannelModTopologyEditor mounts only after a ChannelMod input is loaded and draws Host source coordinates in its own SVG; its extent comes from Host geometry or validExtent, otherwise explicit X/Y is required. TerrainPolygonMapEditor mounts only for a selected, already-loaded PolygonRasterModTerrainInput. It separately captures the project map catalog/tree and the exact persisted PolygonRasterMod visual-context node matching the current Terrain path, sourceVectorIndex and .vis revision, then obtains polygons/CRS/extent through map.terrainInput.render. Its independent SVG camera, selection, tools and manual extent remain local to that view; it does not use the main map selection or fabricate an extent.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: model.terrainTransform and model.terrainTopology project only into the parent ModelDraft. Channel topology operations bind the complete model/sourceState/rows/changedCells, input ID, revision, owner and generation and validate snapshot/sourceRevision/draftIdentity/FIDs/input identity; its load/select/draw/remove/undo/redo/split/moveNodes/moveVertex/insertVertex/deleteVertex/maskRegion/setMetadata commands remain in the parent draft. Polygon map operations load/select/selectAt/stamp/draw/remove/undo/redo similarly bind map/project/XML/session/.vis capture, exact visual-context node, Terrain path/revision and sourceVectorIndex; matching returned topology snapshot/sourceRevision/draftIdentity/feature FIDs are projected into the parent ModelDraft. Host-provided polygon tools preserve source FIDs; unsupported shapes stay disabled, and vertex dragging/panning are not provided. Generic Terrain picker/creator/stats/table remain separate from TerrainMod map editing. Only explicit parent model.save writes Terrain HDF. Static source wiring only; no build or UI acceptance is claimed.

uiMounts.mount: ToolsPageView → USGS terrain tab → USGSTerrainImportControl → USGSTerrainImportDialog / filter / index map / product summary
uiMounts.stateOwner: The workflow is bound to the active Terrain asset, project session/path/XML/revision and source owner. Product filters/selections, stitch choice and per-source inclusion/rounding settings are local to this import review; queries are invalidated when the terrain input changes.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: Download creates Host-owned temporary source files. A user-selected batch then uses model.terrainUSGSDownload, model.terrainInputAppend and status polling; model.save commits the accepted Terrain draft and its HDF revision. model.terrainUSGSCleanup is a separate action requiring a fresh saved-model check that no Terrain input references the temporary paths. Ordinary in-project Terrain sources use their project path/revision/sourceState; only present session-only external references require a captured reference context.

uiMounts.mount: ProjectExplorerControl → NewGeometryDialog / NewBoundaryConditionDialog / NewPlanDialog → useProjectModelCreation
uiMounts.stateOwner: Each dialog owns its field draft and inspection identity. Inspect/commit requests capture project session, path, XML, revision and XML SHA; the accepted receipt also carries the created asset revision and previous project revision.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: modelCreation.commit stages and publishes the new model HDF, adds a PlanAssociation for Plan or optional-source association metadata for Geometry when needed, verifies project/catalog read-back and conditionally rolls back only files whose identity and content still belong to this operation. A Boundary Condition without a primary-key association, or a Geometry with no optional Terrain/N-Value association, can leave project XML and .ras SHA unchanged while the new HDF is identified by assetRevision. The active context changes only after matching parent receipt acceptance.

uiMounts.mount: ProjectExplorerControl → MigrateProjectControl
uiMounts.stateOwner: The modal captures the legacy .prj source path and projectMigration.inspect revision/SHA, plus a separate output directory and the originating project-session context.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: projectMigration.execute invokes the Host converter into a directory separate from the legacy source; the source remains read-only. The output is opened and read back, and only a matching parent-session commit switches the active project. A stale parent may leave the converted output for inspection without changing the current context.

uiMounts.mount: EditorWorkbench → SpatialDataSummaryPage → SpatialDataSummary / SpatialBoundaryConditionsPage → GriddedDataControl → GriddedDataImporter / GriddedDataImporterDialog / GriddedDataImporterSlider / GriddedDataImporterTimeline; SpatialBoundaryConditionRasterImporter uses the importer dialog
uiMounts.stateOwner: Grid requests bind the active Boundary Conditions owner, saved model revision, layer and requested timestep/component. Station/input fields and rows remain in the parent ModelDraft; the spatial page owns its selected layer, frame cache and cancellable frame read.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: model.gridInspect/model.gridFrame inspect sources and read Host frames. Frame selection remains the existing onGridFrame owner. The importer asks for explicit user confirmation and closes only after the workbench confirms. model.gridImport is an immediate saved-model operation against the captured snapshot: it refuses dirty/invalid drafts, requires a changed model revision and imported-grid read-back, then refreshes the parent baseline only after context receipt acceptance. Station/input structure uses model.spatialTransform and remains in the parent draft until model.save. DSS and authenticated Cumulus import are unavailable.

uiMounts.mount: EditorWorkbench → PlanEditorControl → PlanSettingsPage → SchemaPage → SchemaFieldRenderer → PlanTimeWindowModePickerPropertyItem
uiMounts.stateOwner: The Plan schema field ViewModel_SelectedPlan_TimeWindowMode supplies the mode value, choices and field title; the control preserves the enum string and calls the renderer’s existing fieldKey callback. The Host snapshot provides planTimeWindowFieldIDs for mode/start/end and identifies read-only Result Plans.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: Changing mode updates the parent ModelDraft only and does not rewrite start/end. EditorWorkbench groups actual mode/start/end changes into planTimeWindowEdits on the parent model.save transaction. PlanSettings mounts the PropertyItem; NewPlanControl mounts the standalone PlanTimeWindowModePicker, matching the source C# composition. Result Plan fields remain read-only. Current React displays schema choices/current value but does not reproduce the source property header dynamic icon.

uiMounts.mount: GeometryEditor toolbar → “导入线 / 面” → ArcImportDialog → DropTarget / ImportingPreviewList; GeometryEditor → useGeometryWorkbench.inspectVectorImport / applyVectorImport
uiMounts.stateOwner: GeometryEditor supplies the active model, topology snapshot/capture and inspect/apply callbacks from useGeometryWorkbench. ArcImportDialog keeps local browser/server path input, upload receipt, inspected source selection, Merge/NoMerge, MergeContiguousArcs and RemoveExternalArcs options plus request generation. The parent workbench owns topology revision, draftState, draftIdentity, undo and dirty state; responses are accepted only for that still-current capture and exact source family.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: Browser File/FileList selection uses the existing uploadMapSources flow to copy complete Shapefile families into project sources; that upload receipt proves file copying only. Alternatively, users can enter server-visible absolute paths. geometry.vectorImport.inspect captures model/revision/draftState/draftIdentity/paths and Host returns its actual source/family/feature/issue receipt. geometry.vectorImport.apply rereads the selected source families, applies Merge/NoMerge plus MergeContiguousArcs/RemoveExternalArcs and returns a new GeometryTopologySnapshot that enters the same parent topology draft/undo/dirty flow. The Host/UI do not provide a layer attributes or metadata-priority option. Neither upload nor apply writes Geometry HDF; only the parent Geometry page Save persists the draft. This is not map-layer import. Static source wiring only; no batch-9 build or GUI acceptance is claimed.

uiMounts.mount: GeometryEditor → GeometryTopologySummaryPage / GeometryTopologyArcsPage / GeometryTopologyRegionsPage / GeometryTopologyNodesPage → type-specific topology editors; GeometryEditor callbacks → GeometryTopologyTablePage → ConceptualMeshTopologyRegionsEditor → TopologyRecipeBuilder → RecipeBuilder
uiMounts.stateOwner: The Geometry workbench owns the captured model/topology revision, server draftState, undo history and stable row/FID identities. Selected arc/region/node rows are shared with mounted detail and quick-edit controls. The recipe builder is mounted only for selected conceptual-mesh region rows and uses their control-point FIDs; its text/step editing state and inspect/apply request generation are local to that control while identity and draft ownership remain with the parent workbench.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: Supported geometry/topology commands update the current Geometry draft through topology.edit and related point/recipe operations. Recipe inspect calls topology.recipe with the captured model/revision/draftState/controlPointFIDs and optional recipe text; response revision, draftIdentity, FIDs, schema, steps and diagnostics are checked against the active owner. Apply uses topology.edit applyRecipe for the captured control-point FIDs; returned topology snapshot enters the parent draft and existing undo/redo lifecycle, and only parent model.save writes Geometry HDF. Recipe controls expose source-supported ingredient/parameter editors; unknown parameter types remain read-only because Host schema supplies no parameter description. For an existing step, every Host-provided parameter remains in its draft; the source parameter whitelist controls visible form fields and defaults for newly added steps only. Serialization writes the visible parameters in source order, then appends the existing hidden parameters in their original order, so editing or reordering a step does not drop hidden algorithm values. Tag create/set/remove uses selected source FIDs; topology.filter validates owner/revision/draft/FIDs and changes selection only. The overview apply-factor control edits supported all-topology arc/control-point size fields in the same draft; cross-page selected scope is unavailable and node coordinates remain read-only. Geometry save sends fields: {} rather than replaying read-only catalog-summary fields, so Host applies only captured child drafts while preserving parent metadata. These facts are static source wiring; no recipe runtime acceptance is claimed.

uiMounts.mount: EditorWorkbench → TerrainLayersEditor → selected Levee input → LeveeModTerrainInputEditor → LeveeModEditor / LeveeModPropertiesEditor
uiMounts.stateOwner: The active selected Terrain input determines which editors mount: the feature editor requires LeveeModsTable and the property editor requires LeveeModPropertiesEditor/PropertySets. Both use the same selected input projection, schemas and ModelDraft rows/fields.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: Levee fields, table cells and structural transforms update the parent draft/projection; there is no separate Levee file save. The validated parent model.save is the Terrain HDF persistence boundary.

uiMounts.mount: MapFeaturePage → MapLayerTree → RasTreeV2 → MapTreeNode → typed tree nodes; RasProjectMap → RasMapMinimap; MapFeaturePage → ZoomToPointDialog / RasMapPositionIndicator
uiMounts.stateOwner: The active map document and visualization revision own catalog/tree mutations; selected/expanded nodes and viewport/camera are page-local. Typed nodes preserve each catalog node and locator. Minimap and coordinate navigation use the current map viewport and CRS.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: Persisted source visibility goes through map.tree.perform and accepts a matching .vis revision receipt; hidden source members remain in the tree and removal is separate. Minimap panning/zooming, screen-to-world coordinate display and ZoomToPointDialog navigation change only the viewport and do not write .vis or .ras.

uiMounts.mount: SourceManagerControl → AttributeTableEditorControl → AttributeTableDataGrid
uiMounts.stateOwner: The source path and Host capture bind the primary-file canonical path/SHA and complete Shapefile family revision, including required .shp/.shx/.dbf and optional .prj identities. Load and preview transforms recheck the family before and after reading or changing the table.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: attributeTable.load reads the source and attributeTable.transform returns an in-memory table preview for cell/column edits; this flow has no disk-write operation for the Shapefile family. Importing uploaded Shapefile files into a saved map is a separate uploadMapSources/map.vector.importShapefile transaction and may update the map document.

uiMounts.mount: ImportExportToolControl → DepthShapeExporterDialog / RgbTiffExporterDialog → DepthShapeExporter / RgbTiffExporterControl
uiMounts.stateOwner: Depth export captures saved map/Result sources, profile, extent and exact preview parameters; RGB export captures a saved map raster source and inspected source identity. The dialogs bind those receipts to the active project/map owner and invalidate preview when inputs change.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: depthExport.execute writes a Shapefile family and rasterExport.execute writes RGB GeoTIFF only after explicit export action and matching preview. Output paths are absolute paths resolved by the C# Host; Host completion/cancellation receipts describe server-side artifacts and do not imply a browser-local download. This entry records the wired source flow, not runtime validation.

uiMounts.mount: ProjectExplorerControl toolbar → ExternalConnectionManager; RasCatalogInfoPane → ExternalConnectionDetails / DssExternalConnectionPreview → DssCatalogViewer / time-series and paired-data controls → TimeSeriesGraphWindow / TimeSeriesDataTableWindow / PairedDataDataTableWindow → DssDataDialog; project tree → ExternalConnectionCatalogNode
uiMounts.stateOwner: The active project context owns the XML/session/revision identity; external-connection rows and details come from catalog.tree.load in Catalog mode, not the separate project.tree.load project tree. Add/update/remove forms capture the target connection identity and source fields; Result choices come from actual ObservableResult nodes. File paths resolve on the Host machine. Nodes without assetID retain a local tree selection when the active asset is cleared; snapshot reconciliation checks node ID/class/name/path/type, and each project session owns an isolated tree state. The mounted DSS preview subtree comprises DssCatalogViewer/DssFilterControl/PartFilterItemControl, time-series graph and table, paired-data graph and table, and location metadata. The selected catalog record stays keyed by its complete DSS pathname while filtering; each read is bound to the captured file path and catalog SHA/revision. Three full-size DSS dialogs (larger time-series graph, complete time-series table and complete paired-data table) reuse the selected record response and preserve its exact pathname and SHA; opening them does not create a second DSS read/session.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: Add/update/remove use project.connection.inspect then project.connection.commit. Both bind projectPath, projectXml, projectXmlSHA, projectRevision and projectSessionID; commit additionally supplies expectedConnectionSHA256, expectedSourceSHA256 and required expectedSourceReferencesSHA256, plus expectedNormalizedName for add. Inspect returns canCommit/validationMessage, canonicalPath, source and source-reference capture/count, normalizedName, and before/after identities. A Result is written as a native File external connection to its actual Result HDF. Before returning a receipt, Host reopens the project and confirms the connection through CatalogTreeService.LoadCatalog(Mode=Catalog), corresponding to catalog.tree.load; project.tree.load does not contain external connection nodes. The commit receipt carries the new project snapshot and previous revision, before/after identity, sourceCapture, previousSourceReferencesSHA256 and sourceReferencesSHA256; the client validates it before onContextCommit. A remove may capture a disconnected source with nullable path/SHA. DSS preview is read-only. The views render only returned arrays and metadata: NoData breaks graph lines without interpolation, the source time-series table retains returned timestamps/values/quality array (up to 100 visible rows), paired graph/table appears only when paired data exists, and location fields do not infer a CRS or create a map feature. This UI states that its current read path supports DSS 7; DSS 6 is not connected. The three full-size views reuse the already-returned dss.read arrays without another Host call. The time-series table supports paging, jump-to-row and complete CSV copy/download; the paired table includes all returned curves and source array indexes with complete CSV copy/download; the graph dialog enlarges the existing time-series plot. Null values display as NoData and serialize as blank CSV cells; the returned quality array keeps its source order and is displayed separately without inferred sample pairing.

uiMounts.mount: No React Session HDF Add/import UI is mounted; CoreLayerImportDialog is the separate Geometry / Boundary Condition core-layer workflow
uiMounts.stateOwner: There is no React SessionHdfReference registry or Add flow. The web client validates and forwards sessionHdfReferences only when a matching CoreLayerContext is already supplied in a Host asset locator; other catalog/map consumers can process such a supplied context, but the current UI cannot create the capture through Session HDF import.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: The Host registers workspace.import.sessionHdf.inspect to classify Plan, Result or Terrain HDF and MapTreeService accepts map.tree.perform action addSessionHdf when the request carries its exact SessionHdfReferenceCapture in CoreLayerContext. The frontend has no caller for workspace.import.sessionHdf.inspect and no addSessionHdf map-tree action, so users cannot add these captures through the current React UI. SourceManagerControl mounts CoreLayerImportDialog for the distinct workspace.import.coreLayer.inspect/perform flow, whose supported kind contract is Geometry/Boundary Conditions; it is not Session HDF import. The detailed session-HDF reference context, grouping and lifecycle entries in referenceContractScope describe retained source/Host contracts, not a mounted Web workflow. This is a source audit statement, not runtime acceptance.

uiMounts.mount: EditorWorkbench → ClassificationEditor / NValueEditor → ClassificationLayersEditor / ManningsNEditor → source-specific raster, mapping, polygon, constant and classification-layer controls
uiMounts.stateOwner: Classification and Manning views are derived from the current model snapshot plus ModelDraft fields/rows and the selected input/mode. Classification mapping and polygon values and existing Manning interpretation rows stay attached to that parent draft.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: model.classificationTransform reconciles classification fields and mapping rows against the captured snapshot and returns a draft projection; model.manningTransform applies the supported Manning operation against the same model identity. Ordinary edits and accepted projections remain in ModelDraft until model.save. nvalue.preview is read-only. Classification import, mapping-row add/remove, map-click polygon editing, and persisted visualization transparency are not connected.

uiMounts.mount: BoundaryConditionEditor → AirPressurePage → AirPressureHeader / AirPressureControl
uiMounts.stateOwner: The selected Boundary Conditions model snapshot and ModelDraft own the header fields, air-pressure inputs and units. Header and value controls share the same parent field-change callbacks.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: The controls only edit the parent ModelDraft; model.save is the persistence boundary. Unit conversion is local display/input handling and does not create a separate saved asset.

uiMounts.mount: ResultsWorkspace → CrossSectionEditorWindow / CrossSectionEditorControl; ResultsWorkspace → DynamicProfilePlot → ProfileSampleLinePlot / ScrubbedDataDisplay
uiMounts.stateOwner: The standalone cross-section view is bound to the selected project/Geometry source and its classic-geometry file identity; the sample-line view captures the active Result sources and explicit project XY inputs. The scrubber reads the selected result time sample.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: Classic cross sections are read-only station/elevation and bank samples. Dynamic sample lines request Flow or CumulativeVolume at explicit XY points and display each result at its own native times, units and NoData; they do not edit or save a model, do not mean a spatial mesh profile, and do not depend on map clicks. The scrubber displays the actual time/value/unit/NoData sample.

uiMounts.mount: ToolsPageView → tools-tab-sources → SourceManagerControl → VectorImporter → VectorImporterDialog → NewShapefileDialog / ShapefileAttributeTableViewer
uiMounts.stateOwner: The workflow requires a current project map catalog and an explicitly selected saved map. Create requests capture project session/revision, map identity and visualization revision, operation ID, normalized Host destination, shape type and projection. Existing-file import captures the canonical path and complete Shapefile family, including required .shp/.shx/.dbf and optional .prj revisions.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: map.shapefile.create creates a source file and returns a retained creation receipt; that receipt does not mean the map contains the source. map.vector.importShapefile re-captures the exact family and map owner before writing .vis. The UI adopts an imported outcome only after map.document.list/map.tree.load confirms the exact tree locator; stale or uncertain outcomes require a refresh and cannot trigger duplicate creation/import. AttributeTable transform remains a read-only in-memory preview without file write-back. Paths are Host-side, not browser-local. This is a source relation, not runtime acceptance.

uiMounts.mount: ImportExportToolControl → PlanExporterDialog / PlanPickerDialog and ReprojectionToolDialog → ReprojectionToolControl / ProjectionSummary
uiMounts.stateOwner: Plan export captures current project session, selected Plan path, parameters and Host source SHA/revision. Reprojection owns editable coordinate rows and source/target projection choices; identify/transform receipts are validated against row identity and project context.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: planExport.executeDuplex runs only after an explicit export action and rechecks the captured project/Plan/parameters and Host SHA; output path resolution belongs to the Host. reprojection.transform returns coordinate rows and a Host projection receipt but does not write a file. Projection summaries display Host identification/conversion results and never infer a CRS from text. This entry records source wiring, not runtime acceptance.

uiMounts.mount: MapFeaturePage → RasMapElementsOverlay → RasMapLegend → OverlayItem / MapOverlayChrome; MapFeaturePage contextual menu → RasContextualActionsBar; inspector → RasLayerPropertiesPane; MapFeaturePage → RasterSymbologyEditor
uiMounts.stateOwner: The legend is scoped to the active map and exact validated raster source and is populated only from the latest successfully applied Host snapshot. Overlay visibility/folding follows map display settings. The properties pane uses either the selected local feature and its actual layer properties or the selected backend tree node identity/diagnostic. RasterSymbologyEditor also holds the complete Plot Options descriptor map alongside its source-backed style draft; each descriptor keeps the Host PropertyName and is reapplied only for the same raster owner/revision.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: rasterSymbology.apply receives the style draft and actual Plot Options PropertyName/value map, validates the source and .vis identity, renders, then writes the owning map layer and advances visualizationRevision. Standard source-backed RasterSymbology fields preserve legacy .vis serialization; renderer-only PlotRasterTileOutlines is stored in versioned RasterPlotOptions, while ResampleMode uses the existing InterpolationMode field. Non-default recognized options are persisted and default option nodes are omitted. The Host reloads these values into RasterRenderLayer before producing its returned raster; the parent accepts only the prior revision for the same map and source, then refreshes pixels. Palette save/delete remain separate transactions. A legend is published only after a matching apply receipt and refreshed Host snapshot. The local feature pane can zoom to its feature and show CRS/properties; a backend node pane shows type/name/diagnostics and zooms only when a loaded extent exists. This is source contract documentation, not a claim that the route was runtime-tested.

uiMounts.mount: ComputeProofPage → ComputeButton → PauseContinueStop; ComputeProofPage → PlanComputeControl / RealTimeMonitor; ComputeProofPage → OperationResultControl → MessageListControl
uiMounts.stateOwner: ComputeProofPage owns the inspected model identity, one run generation, transport/cancellation state, progress samples, streamed planMessages and terminal result. Streamed messages are accepted only for the active generation and RunId, merged by source message index, and reset on a new run or project/plan identity change. OperationResultControl prefers actual terminal result.messages when present; otherwise it shows the accepted streamed messages. All feedback remains in the current page/run state, with no separate persisted job/message store.
uiMounts.writeBoundary: plan.compute.inspect/execute remain the only inspect and execution operations. ComputeButton mounts PauseContinueStop: Stop uses the existing cooperative cancellation and waits for server terminal confirmation; Pause and Continue are visibly disabled because the current Host exposes no such operations. PlanComputeControl/RealTimeMonitor continue to show actual progress samples; remaining time is explicitly a linear estimate, and the progress-message list is capped to its latest 200 samples with an omitted count. OperationResultControl/MessageListControl show Host message severity, code, evaluated text, log data/target and repeat count; terminal result messages take priority. Raw terminal JSON remains in ComputeSummaryControl. No JobHub feed exists in this web client, so JobHubSummaryButton is not mounted; the source progress dialogs are not represented as solver controls, and chat remains deferred. These are source-wiring facts, not a claim of runtime acceptance.

uiMounts.mount: EditorWorkbench model view (ready Plan/Geometry snapshot) → ModelAssociationsPanel, rendered beside and outside the model form → PlanAssociationsPicker / GeometryAssociationsPicker
uiMounts.stateOwner: The panel is mounted only for an active, ready Plan or Geometry. Its source key captures project session/path/XML/revision, selected model path/kind/revision, model revision, sourceState and any carried core-layer identity. Association choices remain panel-local until commit. The parent blocks edits while the model or another draft owner is dirty/busy and supplies the project-context receipt callback.
readActions: project.association.commit performs a fresh inspect before commit
uiMounts.writeBoundary: Plan choices require project Geometry and Boundary Condition; Geometry choices can independently set or clear Terrain and N-Value. A confirmed terminal consumes its inspection and triggers a fresh source inspection.
Unknown operation status preserves the operation ID and cannot be reported as cancelled.
Validated project coordinates never silently overlay unknown source-coordinate previews.
Map canvas and timeline share one Result frame owner, using native profile indices and times.

referenceContractScope.basis: Retained C# and SwiftUI source relationships and backend contracts
referenceContractScope.interpretation: Porting requirements only; SwiftUI types, macOS capabilities and process details below do not describe current React implementation or establish migrated coverage.

domainRelations.semantics: Rectangular selection, strict quoted TSV and topology context commands share the registered parent draft. Paste respects readonly cells and source validation.
Source feature intersections update the same selected set used by tables. Measurements use world coordinates; final length segments sample real terrain slope with stale-owner rejection.
Saved diagnostics read retained HDF nodes. Unsaved mesh diagnostics use the current child draft; unavailable drafts never fall back to saved cells. Compute writers suspend source reads.
Attribute comparison consumes actual Plan drafts. Matrix generation preserves source option order and holds its mutation lease until actual duplex terminal acknowledgement.
Authentication, clear and URL settings update the shared provider. First-launch secrets stay in memory. Token storage does not invent a missing GPU Hub compute registration.
Actual source providers stage and validate imported projects. Source imports that cannot cancel keep their mutation lease when presentation closes.

Command or Control toggles a true feature set; native list Shift selects a source-ordered range. Replacing or hiding a render owner retires the set. Duplicate source IDs cannot receive edits. Geoprocessing consumes the same captured set.

General line and polygon processing binds a loaded GDB vector leaf, exact persisted sublayer and complete source-directory manifest. Host reopens the exact OGR child and validates the project target CRS before and after the retained operation. Inputs are the actual loaded map feature geometry; GDB remains read only and is never treated as a single file. Existing output staging, cancellation, and stale map/source guards remain the transaction boundary. Capture uses the exact map-owned source rows plus its completed vector-read batch with matching project session and full map workflow identity. A hidden sidebar or different sidebar tree mode does not replace this owner; changed project XML or map/source revisions reject an old capture.

Raster-input operations capture only current checked map rasters, active Result slot/profile sources, or checked visible associated Terrain sources. Map rasters use metadata-only physical extents and real float/double GDAL samplers; Result uses the selected ResultMapResampler profile; Terrain resolves its exact saved/draft map owners and source dependencies. A Result capture requires a settled runtime map frame: for ordinary Result nodes, the active native profile and renderer source-status profile must agree. A successful native profile request installs that frame before asynchronous .vis persistence completes, so Host validates the captured runtime profile against the exact Result block rather than rejecting it because saved .vis still carries the previous profile. MultiResult child slots retain the current key profile's original 10 ms timestamp mapping. Captures reject stale revisions and protected writer paths. No rendered RGBA frame is used as numeric raster data. FlatAreaDetector/LaplacianTerrain clipping choices use no-clip, current map extent, and eligible actual vector/raster/Terrain/Result extents.

Result metadata and appended images live in a persistent parent child draft. Save validates the owner, changes a same-directory Result copy using source Plan.Save, preserves unrelated datasets, atomically publishes, and rebases late edits from the receipt. Discard never writes source HDF.

Checkboxes are transient per-map state and resolve the exact input through the source tree before rendering actual projected coordinates. Source geometry joins the common camera bounds. Uncheck and compute start retire pending reads; this state never writes visualization XML.

A writer callback grants a scoped historical reader lease. Project loaders filter every protected HDF before constructing source models, and revision capture filters before hashing. Normal source reconfiguration remains blocked. Only disjoint historical Result runtimes may refresh; the compute process owns live writer frames.

Actual GDAL metadata validates a real TIFF before a checked source map node is published. The first map and layer are one visualization transaction. File connections stay in the normal project draft. Duplicate, stale and foreign-owner requests cannot mutate the map.

Follow mode propagates exact current feature context; pin freezes that reference but never bypasses source invalidation. A Boundary receiver requires the same canonical file, SHA and line identity. Quick Edit closes before validated Add or View callbacks. Feature selection does not invent a profile-index relationship.

Native overlays restore independent keyed placements, preserve unrelated entries, arrange same-corner peers and retain runtime z order. First-launch application-data suppression passes no serialization key and performs no placement reads or writes.

First-launch uses transient defaults and UID without clearing persisted application data. Ordinary launches reuse the retained UID key. Initial project and crash origin remain explicit launch inputs. Binary stream mode must consume the actual source protocol rather than interpret arbitrary JSON as a map.

Force-set and clear use actual selected source property objects or the topology undo ledger. Live validation replays the captured read-only source state and accepts messages only while text, selection and all owner tokens still match. Geometry output is committed only by parent Save.

The runtime factor scales pen and marker dimensions across map, minimap, boundary and geometry views. It never changes world coordinates, camera scale, persisted source symbology or source unit values. Pure style helpers receive an explicit factor.

WorkspaceStore initializes the generic ToolProvider with its initial nil document and current project session before any tool request, so a first-launch report passes the provider session guard. Categories and service version come from the retained report endpoint. When there is no persisted active project, the normal report may read the first recent saved .ras into an isolated ProjectDocument and capture its canonical path, SHA, XML and Geometry candidates without opening it in WorkspaceStore or mutating drafts. Report invocation, session, recent-selection, compute-state and report-lifecycle changes invalidate that capture; read errors leave the report available without Geometry candidates. Geometry remains unselected until explicit user choice, local capture verifies canonical asset membership and source revisions through the existing Host method, and submission happens only through the explicit native report action. The bounded Modules inventory is collected by the .NET backend process from loaded managed assemblies and enumerated native modules; file-backed modules carry SHA-256 when readable, and the Swift frontend process image is excluded.

Actual query product boundaries share the map transform. The smallest boundary supplies hit metadata and overlap identities. Terrain annotations require an idle primary tool and no Shift modifier, and stale sheets cannot clear a newer owner overlay.

Typed split/node/vertex/mask/metadata operations replay retained source commands. Original outer/hole rings feed even-odd drawing and hit testing. Parent Save owns persistence; stale responses cannot install a different draft.

Readiness uses Plan and exact dirty Geometry/Boundary drafts in the same source Project graph. Ambiguous owners, pending edits, changed revisions and stale replies fail. Inspection never saves or executes queued Prepare.

Wheel zoom preserves the pointer world coordinate using retained factors. Transient editing gates wheel input. Real projection units and ellipsoid metadata drive coordinates and scale. Descriptor help is separate from USGS feature-hit tooltips.

Actual selected import files populate multi-context metadata. Mixed-value ForceSet edits temporary source-equivalent DTOs and never pretends to mutate files or import parameters not consumed by the retained source.

Transient options pass through the actual map.associations.load rendering route. Toggle cancels old frames and invalidates its context token. Original valid/tiled-raster boundaries are painted by the retained renderer; no visualization XML write.

Actual .NET culture-sensitive parsing returns canonical date or TimeSpan components. Async replies revalidate draft ownership; invalid text stays a presentation draft. Existing setters retain original storage/offset/fraction semantics.

Inspector resolves exact visible source rows and typed payloads, with no same-name joins or active-map fallback. Actual selected raster options and supported component actions retain their source owner.
Source menu opens a virtualized editable 1000-by-1000 zero-valued grid and Add Row/Column actions. It is independent of project/solver data.

The source query returns opaque product IDs, the provider's exact DownloadURL and metadata URL, date, resolution and projected footprint. Filtering and map picking operate on that same captured product snapshot. Each download batch preserves per-product raw TIFF path/SHA, provider URLs, helper Float scale, ThirtySeconds rounding, converted resampler-preview TIFF path/GDAL source revision and exact Terrain input ID in each file receipt; the batch receipt binds one cleanup token to the Terrain path, Project path/revision and extent. IsImporting starts false and becomes true only after the complete per-product receipt passes owner validation and is staged. Hide Tile excludes only that exact active Product ID from the pending import and removes its source-rendered preview frame while retaining its TIFF, URLs, receipt and cached frame; Download Tile reactivates the same staged item or downloads it if absent. Query outline visibility is independent. Import Staged sends only currently active raw TIFFs to TerrainInputImportSheet, restores each file's scale and rounding, preserves the original AutoStitchData=true default and the import sheet's Stitch Tiles choice, and excludes hidden products before that choice is applied. If stitching is disabled, the existing importer appends files individually; if the default is kept, it performs its real multi-file stitch. It writes no HDF/project membership until the existing Terrain Add commit succeeds. Query, download, preview and handoff bind project session, map/workflow, exact Terrain editor capture/path/SHA, input ID, extent and request generation; stale results are dropped and the token-owned temporary directory is cleaned after active source reads finish.

domainRelations.source: Terrain channel/levee source rows and selected detail properties
domainRelations.semantics: A table snapshot is not an edit log. Requests carry only explicitly edited row/column IDs; source validation reads their values from the exact submitted rows and leaves other stale row values untouched. Selection is navigation state, scoped to the current input and actual selected feature/property identities. Changing input first stages the previous input draft, then clears its ephemeral selection. Canonical source replies acknowledge applied row cells and selection-scoped fields so old content-derived IDs are not resent; rebased selection acknowledgements refer only to captured source objects. The original discard baseline remains distinct. Detail fields and table cells share the staged parent save without implicit HDF writes.

Selection invalidates the request even when it is navigation only. Actual full-layer samples are dimmed with retained CloneRatioSaturation(.5,.5), with the selected resampler above them in the same world frame. Clearing selection restores full saturation. Original direct ColorMaps.NLCD2011 behavior and its compact-ID color-domain boundary are preserved.

Copied classifications and XY/XYZ/XYM/XYZM ordinate strings enter an exact polygon input after preview. A validated batch is one undo operation; redo retains feature IDs and later class edits. Stale input or malformed batch cannot mutate source files; explicit parent save publishes it. The typed feature clipboard is separate from whole-layer copying and does not claim external generic polygon clipboard compatibility.

Typed source messages retain duplicate entries and ordered log data, separately from progress text and terminal OperationResult summaries. Headless source collection updates use one serialized synchronization context in place of the Windows UI dispatcher, so concurrent reporter callbacks cannot corrupt collection order.
