Deterministic OutputBlock fixtures establish callback integration, not solver acceptance or all active-map chart contexts.

Cell polygons and face polylines come from the selected Result's embedded mesh, including source face internal points. A complete bounded viewport can select the original local cell/face ordinal and request its stored HDF series. Oversized extents require zoom and return no selectable partial geometry. Current project geometry is never substituted. This element picker does not establish the original sample-line cross-section workflow or solver acceptance.

Prepare is distinct from mesh generation. A retained prepare intent runs after topology, mesh, culvert, ordinary field and image edits in the staged parent model. Original property-table and culvert preparation execute there; source failure reason/log are returned without replacing the original HDF or acknowledging any draft. Success reloads the stored source summary and property tables. This action saves only the current geometry, not other project/model drafts.

A local sketch blocks save, discard, close and asset replacement while keeping Apply/Cancel usable. New lines use the real associated terrain extent; reshaping retains source coordinates. Only explicit apply adds an opaque mutation. Failure retains the preview, cancel drops only that preview, and successful geometry edits resample the actual terrain. Ledger undo replays a prefix; it does not discard other geometry children or ordinary fields.

The result route validates one current saved Result and rejects aliases of project models. After confirmation the native service moves that exact file to macOS Trash. Cleanup retires matching result editor sessions, selection and map references even if the originating panel disappears. Serialized result nodes use the validated source Result name rather than the embedded Plan name or a presentation label. A separate catalog action route supports exact-revision operations for its supported Geometry, Plan, Terrain, BoundaryCondition, Classification and NValue assets with dependency-aware deletion checks; this does not broaden Result deletion. The retained Linkage configuration leaves linked hover focus disabled; selection and map-feature highlighting remain independent.

Source maps have no persisted UUID. The workspace binds an in-memory UUID to the serialized map index and type, preserving that UUID during rename. Backend actions update only the current .vis baseline and retain unknown XML. Native acceptance merges Maps/Symbology while retaining unsaved Views and project metadata. Map writers, raster style writers and result removal are mutually exclusive. Source pin serialization is unavailable; Plan/Geometry trees retain the read-only fallback until their map contexts are implemented.

Flow areas retain source row ordinals scoped to the HDF revision; region control points retain source FIDs. Mesh preview overlays the current topology ledger. Original patch rules and source mesh generation run in memory; retained operations join the parent staged save after topology replay. A topology change cannot silently apply an older mesh ledger. Mesh error thresholds and selection are view state.

Culvert field edits and property-set operations replay through original observable APIs. Draft-created property sets retain UUID identities rather than display names. Terrain profiles sample the current actual associated source; association and dependent HDF/raster changes invalidate the old preview without dropping the ledger. Culvert edits share one staged parent HDF publication with topology, mesh, ordinary fields and images.

Result plan, geometry, boundary conditions, compute summary and output-block metadata come from the selected Result file. Same-name current project models do not replace embedded snapshots. Terrain override changes only the current project XML draft; inspection never saves the result. Missing output or compute metadata stays missing.

The profile reader uses actual stored source HDF datasets with original profile timestamps, cell or face identity and the embedded result unit system. Selection and request generations prevent late responses from replacing a different result or element. Empty or absent datasets are explicitly unavailable; source writer fixtures are test data rather than solver acceptance.

Original model defaults are written to a staged source HDF and published under the source project directory without overwriting another file. The project XML draft is carried into model metadata but is not saved implicitly. The creation sheet prevents cancellation during publication; successful output refreshes the actual catalog and opens the correct editor.

Busy topology, mesh or culvert operations cannot be discarded by close, project replacement or application termination. One child's clean callback cannot clear another child or ordinary draft. Old save completion cannot acknowledge a new asset. Save-all still publishes individual files sequentially rather than as one global transaction.

An explicit read-only check applies canonical plan time-window state and ordered events plus ordinary draft fields against current project XML. Source CanCompute returns actual result, codes, severities, ordered log values and aggregated counts. Selected model dependency hashes and existence states are checked before/after. A reply cannot install after edit, reload, discard, association change or source revision change. Checking neither saves nor prepares a solver job.

Arc polylines, completed-region outer/inner rings, control points and nodes use actual source coordinates. Compound region boundaries retain source row selection IDs without inventing a single FID. Even-odd rendering/hit testing preserves holes. Pan/zoom remain view state; tag/size refresh keeps camera extent and existing child draft save semantics.

Typed BaseUnitType IDs identify source/display units without guessing a family from unit labels. Temporary calculator edits call the retained conversion service; cancel does not write. Explicit apply revalidates original owner, field, unit and raw value before scoped draft commit. Interval normalization preserves the original 100 ns TimeSpan rounding; display formatting does not truncate stored precision.

The shell displays every current message with severity, title, body, timestamp and per-item dismissal. Source timeout scales UTF-16 length and clamps to 25..100 percent of ten seconds. Hover pauses remaining lifetime, disappearing suspends timers, dismissed/expired IDs do not replay; history stays in the workspace. Caller-supplied actions use actual Messages navigation rather than a generic success stub.

Source FIDs identify features independently of sorted rows. Typed tags, metadata, Arc and Region user-defined column add/rename/delete, and quick sizing replay against the original geometry in memory. Column permissions use the source Arc or ControlPoint default-column predicate and observable metadata-table APIs; Nodes expose no column CRUD. Arc sizing follows its Constant or Count function; regions and Quad sides use their source rules. The child draft joins ordinary geometry fields and images in one staged HDF save. Save locks the child, acknowledges only its captured draft and rebases its revision. Discard, model replacement and late replies cannot restore an obsolete draft.

Catalog and professional project trees have separate source hierarchies and separate sessions. Current unsaved XML supplies associations. Model nodes retain actual asset paths, backups and source component identities. Maps retain their own IDs and original types. Unsupported tree mutations remain unavailable rather than reporting a saved change.

The visualization node supplies original relative-first filenames. Every source request validates its exact map and node and samples the actual GDAL raster through retained resampling and color-fill logic. Apply renders actual pixels before atomically publishing visualization XML. Custom palettes share the original global catalog. Native baseline acceptance verifies old and new visualization revisions and preserves unsaved Views. Source-map IDs isolate pixels and extents between maps; source changes require an explicit reload.

The retained BaseUnitType catalog defines compatible families and performs conversion. Editing the source value converts forward; editing the target value or changing its unit converts backward. Changing the source family invalidates incompatible target choices. G8 is presentation only; raw input and full stored values survive formatting and invalid intermediate input.

Opt-in newline JSON streams source messages and actual reported percentages while legacy responses remain supported. Pipe chunks are buffered as bytes until a whole frame is available. Exactly one terminal response is accepted. Cancellation terminates the actual request child and late UI callbacks are ignored. The migration result preserves source messages and checks the project revision again before presenting an explicit Open action.

Mode and date changes replay in order through the retained observable setters. Opaque source state preserves inactive internal dates while boundary inheritance displays actual boundary dates. Time-window fields bypass generic dirty-field overlay. Refresh baseline excludes user state; discard restores that baseline. Save acknowledges only captured event IDs and rebases later events onto the new saved source revision.

The selected asset loads its own source summary schema and metadata through the existing model provider. This read does not register an editor or replace any editor draft. N-value and classification kinds derive from actual source schemas. Stale selection replies cannot overwrite the current summary; professional previews require real selected-node render data.

Inspect validates the retained v6 project header and proposes an unused output folder. The retained ModelConverter writes a separate project; success requires one top-level RAS file. Cancellation terminates the one-request backend child and may retain partial output. The current workspace and drafts stay live until success; replacement confirmation happens after the migration sheet dismisses.

The source editor displays only MaxValue and MinValue using three-significant-digit NumberConverters formatting. A provider must supply the actual fill color values; generic raster limits or editable palette draft stops cannot substitute for that context.

Project maps follow loaded project layers. Buildable maps begin empty and include only explicitly added layer IDs. URL import and tree drop capture the destination map; hidden layers, viewport and membership stay per map. Professional model tree listeners remain unconnected.

Refresh evaluates source getters against current unsaved project XML without writing any files. Baseline excludes user drafts; draft applies validated setters. Aliases, exact raw input and images remain dirty. Old replies cannot replace later typing, reload, discard or save; association changes during save are deferred.

Priority display reverses real source order. Local selection is navigation-only. Renames, functional expressions, constants and extents are scoped drafts. Source transforms preserve the original discard baseline. Removed rasters remain in the dependency ledger. Explicit staged HDF save rebases selected input identity and resets the source layer input hash. Source sampling provides the actual raster preview; unsupported input types remain intact.

Keep per-source UI structure review separate from backend execution and native/browser acceptance; an unreviewed control is not assumed absent. The retained-source resources/editor-schemas.json resource available in this Web checkout records a historical 517-entry resource-backed C# UI baseline with stable source paths, plus 224 schemas and 9 tables. It excludes supplementary code-created controls and backing/support objects; the original audit-ui-rewrite.py belongs to the retained-source repository and is not present here. The 517 baseline is therefore a valid source reference, but not by itself a total-UI denominator or a measure of current React implementation. A comparable status count requires a deduplicated stable source-ID inventory mapped to actual mounted React paths and manually classified behavior; basename matches and schema extraction alone do not establish a translated screen or feature.

Chrome collapse, move, resize, placement, opacity and visibility are view state. Undo/redo is enabled only when a provider supplies actual edit history capabilities. Scale labels remain map-coordinate units until a real projection-aware length conversion is provided; do not infer metres from project display units.

The retained layer samples a 256x256 presentation raster from current source inputs and drafts. Colors map actual class names, NoData is transparent. Map replies are scoped to asset/load/edit revisions; source raster dependencies are rechecked. Fit/pan/zoom are navigation, not model edits.

Create/replace/delete mutate actual source polygons in memory. Batch delete is one undo step. Original feature IDs survive earlier deletions; new features receive GUIDs. Replay preserves class overrides and independent metadata. XY edits retain optional Z/M arrays and nonfinite ordinate strings. Drawing selects only new features; save rebases feature selection by source/input ordinal. Explicit source HDF save establishes a new undo baseline; discard restores saved geometry.

Mixed lists retain individual Z/M flags in optional Has Z/Has M attributes with compatible coordinate matrices. NaN fillers never invent an actual Z dimension for M-only features. Missing flags retain legacy dimension inference; float XYZ is decoded. Source regression covers mixed polygons/polylines and legacy layouts.

Inspection reads actual pixels/polygons/string attributes without writing. Source discrete TIFF conversion supplies owned copied inputs and original NLCD class labels; shapefiles append real polygons and selected string attributes to the source polygon input. Import saves captured model drafts and new inputs through a staged HDF. Failed batches remove only owned new rasters. Native sheet identity carries selected files atomically.

Stable editor IDs derive from asset revision and original input ordinal. Selection is navigation-only; reorder/removal preserve independent field/table drafts and the original discard baseline. Polygon inputs remain nonremovable. Explicit save rebases IDs while retaining the selected source input.

Raster integer keys are immutable; only source class names change. Polygon class names and constant values edit actual source objects without replacing geometry. Names persist from input definitions; mapping/name hashes participate in source dirty detection and reset after successful save. Raster dependency SHA checks guard structural transforms and staged HDF saves.

Classification choices use file paths; HDF persists source names. Opening does not reconcile or prune mappings. Explicit changes use original class-map reconciliation, preserving common values and adding new names with zero. None clears the actual association and table.

The original twenty NLCD values update matching names only; custom classes remain unchanged. Operations retain metadata/image drafts and the saved discard baseline. Explicit save writes the actual HDF table; dependency hashes reject changed classification files.

Retained GDAL summaries and selection builders supply actual bands. The source scalar/vector/precipitation importers write canonical values and timestamps; independent wind components and NoData are preserved.
A frame changes only its spatial presentation. It cannot install draft fields as a saved baseline or replace point/payload state. Import is an explicit model-save operation.

One source station can be referenced by multiple layer inputs. Name/coordinates/optional height edit the shared object. Removing or replacing a station clears both object and saved-name references across all five layers; input values remain intact.

Scalar station values and both wind components retain original units. Regular times are derived; absolute/relative irregular arrays retain subsecond precision. Charts cannot be sent as edits for table-backed pages. Station/input structural records remain in the editor draft until explicit HDF save.
Project owns collections; a catalog/tree node is a separate presentation identity.
Project XML stores names; the project resolves actual object references.
Missing and removed references must remain distinguishable.
Boundary association changes derived compute times.
Editable project geometry uses explicit associations.
No implicit project-default fallback in ordinary Geometry.AssociatedTerrain.
Use the explicit source association.
Defaults are source-specific, not a universal association rule.
Classification mode needs its source classifier and interpretation table.
The table and classifier participate in versioning and resampling.
Display priority can reverse source order; map moves through the source collection.
Source collections and actual feature/property-set identities determine detail edits.

Real source lines and payloads supply names, enablement and editor types. Hydraulic enablement uses source SetHydraulicPayload. Source constructors and AddPayload/RemovePayload operate in per-editor drafts. Constants, regular/irregular/spatial tables, remote connection metadata, existing rating curves and base descriptions are connected. Functional formula editing/evaluation remains unavailable in the source.

Editor GUIDs map original ordered source lines/payloads without using display names. State belongs to one asset SHA and editor; ordered creation/removal records replay over baseline identities. Explicit save adopts current identities and clears structural records. State never enters HDF. External changes reject stale edits.

Regular, absolute/relative irregular and spatial source series are connected. Missing values travel as nullable Y. Regular dates are derived; irregular dates are editable. Spatial rows are canonical and plot samples cannot overwrite table edits. Source clear/interpolation/add-station run in memory until explicit model save.

Rating curves preserve input variable, count, offsets and real arrays. Functional mode preserves only existing base metadata; no formula is invented. Complete irregular row arrays can grow/shrink while untouched timestamps retain precision.

Shared boundary time-window fields alias actual source properties. Fixed-start toggle writes the real timestamp/null sentinel; computed actual dates remain read-only. Preview updates derived values without recording them as user edits.
Do not substitute current project models sharing the same display names.
Override, exact signature, signature name, then project default; exact API only matches signatures.
Current source Result.AssociatedNValueLayer uses Project.DefaultNValueLayer.
Actual output data drives result maps, time series and profiles.
Unsaved project metadata affects source reads without writing the project file.

The native picker uses actual source paths and exports current project associations without saving project XML. Source migration includes the selected Plan, geometry, boundary, terrain, Manning/classification and required external connections; relative copied connections remain relocatable. Source and acknowledged ZIP destination hashes guard local publication, and creation and export share the project-operation lease. A committed ZIP receipt binds canonical project and Plan paths, project session, source revision, optional CoreLayer identity token, output path, SHA-256 and byte length. Optional model-library upload is a second stage, available only for ZIP exports with existing developer S3 credentials and an explicit Model ID; the captured owner is the application UID or the source fallback anonymous. The Host rechecks the receipt and ZIP bytes before ModelLibraryClient.PushAsync(force:false). Duplex progress and cancellation cover both stages, while cancellation or failure after local commit preserves the ZIP and session receipt. Directory exports cannot be uploaded.

HDF fixed widths count UTF-8 bytes; all bounded writes retain complete scalar values and adjacent fields. UTF-8 type markers, variable-string offsets, compound readers and attribute names preserve Chinese paths and connection names. Failed model input saves propagate and leave project XML uncommitted; they do not drop input definitions.

Source constructors and HDF writers create geometry, boundary conditions and plans. Choice IDs are source paths; project XML retains name associations. Native dates retain instants, plans inherit boundary windows or show source custom-window warnings. A staged no-overwrite publication creates only one model; matching associations join the existing project draft, preserving unknown XML. Project replacement, save and quit wait for publication. Unsupported tools remain unavailable.
Legacy history retains unknown access times. Counts use the five source folders; removing history preserves project files. Old preview replies cannot resurrect removed records.

Original ShapefileIO loads actual source data; source Table/ObservableTable applies working cell/column edits. IDs survive column rename/removal. Raw null/type/name values remain distinct. Boolean/null choices enter drafts synchronously. CSV export flushes those drafts and freezes mutations across the native save panel, then acknowledges only a completed write. Owned tasks cancel the child request; close and termination guard independent windows.

Runtime identity follows the XML object instead of a list index. File previews bind project, connection definition, directory and path mappings; stale/closed replies cannot replace current data. Batch file names validate before any XML mutation.
Create/apply require source evaluation of the current input. Geographic CRS is rejected by source project rules. PRJ paths normalize to embedded WKT after actual source parsing.
Area identifiers are not CRS identifiers. Resolve PROJ usage before returning actual EPSG choices; canonical names, aliases and code search share the portable source reader.
Source flow-area identity owns cell count, metadata and degree-error rows.
Loading, mixed types, empty and active sizing come from source state; direction scopes are distinct.
Local text is not model data. Apply/mode/ratio commands return explicit source mutations; display-only fields never enter saved edits.
Names do not identify datasets. Native plots separate source axis pairs; raw samples and display NoData handling remain distinct.
Actual profile IDs differ from slider positions. Source requests serialize/coalesce; frame buffers and preview stay in the owning map and preserve its world viewport.
Running source values are observed with real UI timestamps, bounded to 10000 points and reset per model/job identity; no solver history is inferred.
Each session owns its baseline and source revision.
Backend fieldGroups synchronize fields across pages by actual property identity.
EditorRow.fieldBindings connects cells and object detail drafts.
Stable scopes survive sort/filter and prevent cross-object edits.
Viewport, visibility, tool and preview are separate for each map.
Actual provider owns mutations, undo/redo and authoritative results; production provider pending.

Tree selection, asset selection and feature selection are not interchangeable. Same-project, same-map and same-mode refreshes retain valid selected and expanded node identities while validating them against the new snapshot; changed owners or missing identities clear selection. A visualization style write must refresh locators without pretending HDF model assets changed.
NValue and classification nodes come from retained HDF groups, never filenames. Unrecognized HDF files remain visible. Replies are scoped to the current project and asset revision.

Five source spatial layers persist enablement, type, ratios and scalar/vector constants. Equal property names on different layers are not aliases. Observable construction never resets stored weather values.
Changed parameters invalidate execution eligibility.
Include detached windows; save-all is not a multi-file transaction.
Retain source metadata, remove actual datasets, refresh IDs after saving.
Do not clear later input when an earlier request completes.
Cancel work and remove completed records are distinct commands.

The standalone coordinate tool preserves source and destination choices (Project, WGS84, Web Mercator and Custom), raw custom EPSG/Proj4/WKT text, editable X/Y input rows and ordered result rows. The retained projector transforms each complete finite pair; blank, invalid, failed and unavailable rows remain distinct. The dialog starts with ten rows and adds five. Source identification checks candidate files in order and embeds recognized WKT; it does not modify project/model files. Typed summaries expose parsed validity, units, projected/vertical flags, EPSG and UTM metadata, plus finite area-of-use bounds when the retained projection supplies them; Local/null projections do not receive fabricated bounds. Stale project, projection, side or row replies cannot replace current results.

The action captures one exact project Boundary Condition, its current model draft and project XML, then validates one selected result path/revision and the optional timestamp as raw text. Explicit Attach and Save records the result as one shared Stage and Velocity source; the retained PrepareForCompute path performs the later data ingestion. The host stages model and project XML changes under one operation ID and returns an exact receipt; status/retry recovers an ambiguous commit, while only a confirmed notFound operation can be safely canceled. Closing the sheet retains the operation in the same running app, and a workspace banner reopens its cached session while the mutation lease protects the owning editor. The backend journal survives backend interruption; recovery requires the original request context and operation ID, and no frontend process-restart discovery route is implemented. This entry records source transaction behavior, not native acceptance or ingestion success.

The standalone calculator keeps SBTM, ISBTM, STAB and STATE inputs as raw strings and calls the retained four calculation paths independently, with section-specific input issues and unavailable results. Source tables, outputs and chart series are projections of those results; editing inputs marks calculations stale and does not write a project, HDF or map. Case IDs identify current source positions rather than names. BTM import requests confirmation before either appending on a matching grain grid or replacing STAB cases when grids differ; the response acknowledges whether existing cases were replaced. Static source wiring does not establish build, regression or native-window acceptance.

The selected GDAL dataset is identified by its canonical root and every local file GDAL reports, including VRT dependencies; virtual /vsi sources are rejected because their local bytes cannot be verified. Actual band count and data type select the retained single-band, RGB image or discrete renderer. Preview and map load revalidate the full manifest. The .vis node retains the source and map type; no raster conversion or snapshot is created. Local project projections remain valid and do not gain fabricated CRS metadata.

One canonical directory manifest covers actual non-lock files for both OGR vector layers and GDAL raster subdatasets. Preview, publication, rendering and edits verify the same manifest. Persist the dataset parent and exact typed child: vector children identify the source layer, while raster children retain the GDAL connection string and reopen only within a verified dataset lifetime. Vector records preserve source feature order, IDs, field types, set versus NULL state, XYZM and ring roles.

Inspect accepts actual polyline and polygon Shapefiles in the owning Geometry project coordinates. Apply re-reads selected source families, verifies the same source and draft identity, and submits the imported features as one replayable topology mutation. Merge-contiguous and external-arc options are part of that mutation. Undo/discard remain in the topology child ledger; only the registered parent Geometry save writes HDF.

The retained writer creates the family in a sibling staging directory. Validate the map, destination and every staged member and prepare the in-memory receipt before publishing sidecars; rename .shp last as the commit point. Never clobber an existing family. Synchronous rollback removes only this operation’s published members whose bytes still match; the current SwiftUI session keeps the create receipt so a failed map import can retry without invoking the writer again.

The export uses the selected source raster, its persisted symbology and retained RasterRenderLayer/RgbTiffExporter algorithms over the requested full extent or current view. Progress and duplex cancellation belong to the export operation. Recheck source and .vis revisions before a no-clobber atomic single-file publish, and return a receipt computed from the staged TIFF. A Local projection may evaluate successfully with no Projection object: retain geotransform and omit CRS rather than inventing one.

Require the explicitly selected active Result or MultiResult owner, selection slot zero and a stored profile; never substitute another Result or choose a first owner. Preview and export use the retained depth render layer, Mapper with AllowNegativeDepths, ResultMapResampler and contour generation with the captured cell size and simplification. Recheck result and terrain dependencies, respond to duplex cancellation, compute every sidecar receipt before family publication and rename .shp last. A valid Local projection writes no fabricated .prj.

The project format does not persist an external core-layer reference. Each capture is session-only and binds kind, source path, canonical path, source SHA, name and reference ID; a matching typed context must be supplied explicitly whenever a backend request rebuilds Project. Without that context a Project-rebuilding request does not discover or attach arbitrary external references. Existing explicit standalone model-path requests retain their contract and do not register a project reference. The Swift registry clears on session/path replacement and rebases references after successful source saves. Add Reference acts on the exact selected map; Copy File copies bytes without implicitly changing map membership.

The stable entry owner is project session plus map ID and actual map type; the full workflow and map identity form a separate mutable capture epoch. An epoch change cancels old evaluation and re-inspects the new capture while retaining the same owner’s recipe, name, visibility and profile. Re-evaluate only if every input still matches source ID, revision, availability, kind and map type; otherwise clear its layer and full-source extent while keeping the editable entry with an error. Reference points are the visible entries’ whole-source min/max corners, never current viewport corners. An open editor retains unsaved recipe, input, constant, name and profile drafts across changes to the same stable owner. Adopting a changed source version requires explicit confirmation for the same source ID, kind and map type. Add/Save always inspect current sources, evaluate and post-inspect the same context before registry commit; every asynchronous stage fences operation generation and draft revision.

Both canvas hits and filtered feature rows capture the same menu context and share one action dispatcher. Preserve an already-selected set or add under Control. Resolve row and layer by exact identity; changed project XML, visualization or Core context invalidates an old menu even while the previous rendered rows remain cached.

Read the actual OutputBlock.Times and Flow or OutletVelocity for each selected source barrel ordinal. Keep source units and NoData; never replace a time series with a single-frame particle profile or a spatial sample. Close and source changes retire pending loads; retain already-read chart data with a stale indication.

Replay the captured parent-owned drafts without saving the Geometry. Find returns exact coordinates and source viewport for a cell, face or node. Export actual centers or perimeter polylines with typed original attributes and project CRS. Prepare artifact receipts before no-clobber publication and preserve them after commit, even if UI currentness or cleanup subsequently fails.

Grid-only dateless A/B/C/F grouping retains UnCondensedPaths. Read a private DSS copy; stable identities retain original source path and SHA. Scalar imports one complete series; wind uses distinct complete X/Y series from one file with matching times, grid and units. Source checks surround reading and staged HDF commit; duplex cancellation and publication share a lock. Recheck the target HDF revision after all dependency reads and inside that lock immediately before replacement. A winning commit returns its receipt.

Deliver the committed canonical snapshot using the captured asset before editor-generation guards. Closed editors can rebase only the exact captured Core reference in the same project; replacement references and new editors are never overwritten. UI snapshot installation remains guarded by original asset and load generation.

Cell and Face curves read the current Geometry child draft for the exact captured Geometry owner. When property tables are missing, the user may explicitly run the existing child-session computation from the chart. The workspace owns that operation lifetime and progress/cancel UI; on success it verifies the same project session, CoreLayerRequestContext, asset/model/path/revision, topology, Flow Area and selection, captures the new draft SHA, then re-finds the same element before Host replay and chart loading. Parent Geometry save remains the final HDF persistence boundary, not a prerequisite for plotting. Node curves are unsupported.

At the explicit inspect action, capture the selected saved map request, accepted Result snapshot, selection overrides, project session, CoreLayerRequestContext, map workflow identity and exact Geometry owner. Reuse that immutable capture after awaits and reject changed owners or snapshots. Host matches the same FlowAreaIndex, FlowArea ID/name, mesh hash and cell/face counts, then verifies every returned series against an accepted slot-0 locator, result path and revision. No accepted snapshot means no query. Chart data is read-only and is not a model/HDF save transaction.

Retained postprocessing algorithms operate in a unique temporary derived cache for each UI reader. Independent backend processes do not create, delete or transpose the shared default PostProcess.h5. Dispose all cache HDF resources before removing the private directory; original Result bytes remain unchanged.
